newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices slip with crude, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices slip with crude, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly continued to slide Thursday in lackluster trade, plagued by further weakness in crude and forecasts for more unseasonably-mild East Coast weather, industry sources said.
"There's' not much buying interest with everything (crude and natgas) down," said one cash trader, adding mild weather forecasts have killed prospects for any East Coast utility demand near-term.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was little changed at about $21.25 a barrel, but November and December paper fell almost 50 cents with crude to about $20.65-90.
High sulphurs in New York slipped 25 cents, with 2.2 percent now talked at $20.25-50, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was unchanged at about $19.75, while three percent fell 25-50 cents to about $19 on prospects for better supplies and softer bunkers there.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

Mild weather pressured New York City gate gas prices almost 15 cents lower Thursday to the low-$2.80s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent. November New York gas also weakened to about NYMEX plus 55-60 cents, or in the $3.05-3.10/mmBtu area versus a resid paper equivalent of $3.29.
